messages:
maria: Quick sync 7 we need a pragmatic control-plane tenancy model that balances isolation, cost, and operability. Two directions: full per-tenant CP slices vs shared CP with strict tenant quotas. Thoughts?
ben: Per-tenant slices are the safest for blast radius but huge infra & release overhead. Also painful for cross-tenant features.
oliver: Shared CP with enforcement seems more realistic. Main risk: noisy tenants can still impact tail latency unless we have strong isolation primitives.
lei: Could do a hybrid: shared control plane + small reserved fast-path pool for committed tenants + tenant-level quota enforcement for everyone else.
maria: Agree hybrid might give the best tradeoff. Key requirements: clear billing signals, small blast radius, and easy rollbacks.
ben: Implementation idea: add a cp-quota-enforcer per CP node (sidecar) that does token-bucket per-tenant and emits meter events. If tenant exceeds, either route to reserved pool (if assigned) or reject with 429.
oliver: For routing: need a priority-routing table that marks which tenants can use reserved_pool. The router should prefer reserved_pool for those tenants when under burst. Also need an admission controller for global headroom.
lei: Observability: emit tenant_id, req_type, token_estimate, cpu_ms, cp_node_id, and throttle_reason. That allows us to attribute cost and debug noisy tenants without full slices.
maria: Rollout plan suggestion: feature-flagged canary -> 5% nodes -> add metrics for tail latency and error rates -> increase. Start reserved_pool opt-in with 3 committed customers.
ben: Also define degradation tiers: reserved_pool > shared-best-effort > low-priority background (batch) where we can shed. Expose a throttle_reason string in traces so users can diagnose throttles.
oliver: Capacity planning: reserved_pool capacity should be shared across tenants with non-overlapping peaks. We can use historical peak-fit to pack tenants onto reserved nodes.
lei: Security/data residency: design token format so telemetry hooks can be swapped out for private deployments. If a tenant migrates to Private, CP telemetry should be forwardable or suppressable.
maria: Edge cases: large correlated spikes from many small tenants could still overwhelm shared CP. Need a global circuit-breaker that steps in and favors SLA customers.
ben: Agree. Add a graceful degradation policy: 1) reserve pool for committed customers, 2) throttle non-committed, 3) shed batch work. Also add auto-escalation alerts when global throttle rates exceed X%.
oliver: Testing: create surge test harness that simulates N tenants ramping quickly. Validate that reserved tenants keep latency, others get 429s with Retry-After and metrics.
lei: Action items:
- maria: draft mini-RFC for hybrid model (quota-enforcer API, router policy, metrics schema)
- ben: sketch SRE capacity plan and packing algos
- oliver: add surge test scenarios + rollout gates
- lei: metrics/tracing spec and telemetry hooks for private deployment
oncall-bot: deploy-notify: cp-quota-enforcer v0.4 canary started on 5% of CP nodes.
maria: OK assigning reviewers @ben @oliver @lei. I'll include a short rollback playbook. Any objections?
ben: LGTM.
oliver: LGTM.
lei: LGTM, will follow up with metrics PR.
oncall-bot: reminder: add cp-router changes to next week's rolling deploy schedule.
